Estimate a distal outcome's mean in each latent class

Source: R/three-step.R
three_step.Rd

Estimates the mean of an outcome in each latent class of a fitted model, or the difference between every pair of classes, by the three-step approach, and returns a data.frame. The measurement model is fitted first, units are assigned to classes, and the outcome is then related to the assignments with a correction for classification error, so the outcome does not influence the classes. "bch" weights give approximately unbiased class means; regressing on the modal class attenuates the differences (Vermunt 2010; Bakk and Vermunt 2016).

Usage

three_step(
  x,
  data,
  outcome,
  level = c("individuals", "groups"),
  method = c("bch", "proportional", "modal"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  contrast = c("none", "pairs"),
  adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
  vcov_type = c("cluster", "independent")
)

Arguments

x

A covariate-free fitted multilpa() or lta() model, or a trajectory model that classifies persons (mixture_regression() with class_level = "group", with or without random effects) fitted without membership covariates. Fits with membership covariates and multilevel growth mixtures (cluster) are refused with latents_unsupported_three_step: the correction uses a fixed, unconditional classification-error matrix and independent units.

data

The data frame carrying the outcome, in the fit's row order. Columns shared with the fit are checked row by row; a frame with too little identifying information raises a warning that alignment cannot be verified. For a trajectory model it must be the data frame the model was fitted to.

outcome

Name of a numeric outcome column, without missing or infinite values, that is not a measurement indicator of x. For level = "groups" it must be constant within each group, and for a trajectory model within each person.

level

"individuals" (default) relates the outcome to profiles, "groups" to group classes. For a trajectory model the outcome is related to its person classes, reported with level = "persons"; "groups" is refused there with latents_bad_argument.

method

"bch" (default) applies the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars weights; "proportional" weights by the posterior probabilities (attenuated); "modal" uses the uncorrected modal assignment, for comparison.

ci_level

Confidence level for the intervals (default 0.95).

contrast

"none" (default) reports one outcome mean per class; "pairs" reports the difference between every pair of classes, with a test against zero.

adjust

Multiplicity correction across the pairwise differences, passed to stats::p.adjust(): "BH" (default), "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY" or "none". Ignored for contrast = "none".

vcov_type

"cluster" (default) sums the influence contributions within the fit's groups and treats the groups as the independent units, as required when the outcome is measured on observations nested in groups. "independent" treats every observation as an independent unit, which is appropriate only without nesting (for example a fit with a single group). The choice is recorded in the result's vcov_type attribute.

Value

A base data.frame. For contrast = "none", one row per class with the columns level, method, class, estimate, standard_error, conf_low, conf_high and effective_n; class means are not tested. For contrast = "pairs", one row per pair of classes with the columns level, method, class, reference_class, estimate (the mean of class minus the mean of reference_class), standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low and conf_high, as in r3step(). A contrast with zero standard error has NA_real_ statistic and p-values.

The result's vcov_type attribute records the variance used; for contrast = "pairs" the adjust attribute records the correction applied to p_adjusted.

Details

The correction assumes the outcome is independent of the assigned class given the true class. On an lta() fit, level = "individuals" uses one row per occasion and relates the outcome to the profile at that occasion, with the default group-clustered variance accounting for the repeated occasions within a group. This is a marginal profile-outcome analysis, not a model of outcome effects on transitions or of a sequence-level outcome.

The cluster-robust variance is the sum of one outer product per independent unit, scaled by the small-sample (CR1) factor G / (G - 1) for G units (groups, or observations under vcov_type = "independent"). These contributions sum to zero at the estimate, so the variance has rank at most G - 1: it is zero with a single group and singular with as many groups as classes. Both cases are refused with latents_too_few_groups; vcov_type = "independent" gives the unclustered variance.

The classification-error matrix is treated as known, so the intervals are too narrow. Over 60 replications of a two-profile design with 8% misclassification and a true class difference of 10, "bch" had a bias of -0.13 (against -1.28 for "modal" and -1.82 for "proportional") and its nominal 95% intervals covered the true difference in 85% of replications; the intervals of the other two methods covered it in none.

References

Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: two improved three-step approaches. Political Analysis, 18, 450–469. Bakk, Z., & Vermunt, J. K. (2016). Robustness of stepwise latent class modeling with continuous distal outcomes. Structural Equation Modeling, 23, 20–31.

Examples

set.seed(11)
group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10)
truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5)
example_data <- data.frame(
  g = group,
  a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0))
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,
                n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1)
three_step(fit, example_data, "y")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n
#> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  -----------
#>     1  -0.069  [-0.463,  0.326]  0.20       182.75
#>     2   9.972  [ 9.531, 10.412]  0.22       170.37
three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs")
#> Distal outcome: class differences (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class  vs  Difference         95% CI      p  p (BH)
#> -----  --  ----------  -------------  -----  ------
#>     2   1       10.04  [9.36, 10.72]  <.001   <.001
